chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Abu Baseer, and Bureyd, and Al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the sheep: for every forty sheep, one sheep is due, and there is nothing due for what is below forty. Then there is nothing due until it reaches one hundred and twenty; when it reaches one hundred and twenty, one sheep is due in the same manner. When it exceeds one hundred and twenty, two sheep are due.

There is nothing more than two sheep until it reaches two hundred; when it reaches two hundred, it is due in the same manner. When it exceeds two hundred by one sheep, three sheep are due. Then there is nothing more than that until it reaches three hundred; when it reaches three hundred, three sheep are due. When it increases by one, four sheep are due until it reaches four hundred.

When four hundred is complete, one sheep is due for every hundred, and the previous rule is dropped. There is nothing due for what is below one hundred after that, and there is nothing due for the 'nayyif' (the surplus between the hundreds).
And they both said: For everything upon which the year has not passed while it is with its owner, there is nothing due. When the year passes over it, it becomes obligatory.

key_terms.الشَّاةِ: Sheep (specifically referring to the animal subject to Zakat)
key_terms.النَّيِّفُ: The surplus or remainder (specifically the sheep between the hundreds, e.g., 101-119)
key_terms.الْحَوْلُ: The lunar year (period of time required for Zakat to become obligatory)

ai.seo_question: What is the Zakat ruling for a herd of sheep in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the precise nisab and calculation method for Zakat al-An'am, emphasizing that the obligation is contingent upon the lunar year (hawl) passing while the herd remains in the owner's possession. Shia scholars highlight the distinction between the initial complex tiered structure (40, 120, 200) and the simplified rate of one sheep per hundred after reaching 400, reflecting the juristic principle of avoiding excessive burden on smaller herds.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim, and Abu Baseer, and Bureyd and Al Fuzayl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the sheep: ‘Regarding every forty sheep, is one sheep (as Zakāt), and there is nothing regarding what is below forty. Then there would be nothing regarding it until it reaches one hundred and twenty. So when it does reach one hundred and twenty, so regarding these would be similar to that one sheep. So when it exceeds upon one hundred and twenty, so regarding these would be two sheep.

And there would be nothing more than two sheep until it reaches two hundred. So when it does reach two hundred, so regarding these would be similar to that. So when it exceed upon two hundred by one sheep, so regarding these would be three sheep. Then there would not be anything more than that until it reaches three hundred. So when it does reach three hundred, so regarding these would be three sheep similar to that. So when it exceed by one, so regarding these would be four sheep until it reaches four hundred.

So when the four hundred is complete, that would be upon every one hudred, one sheep, and the former matter would be dropped. And there is nothing upon what is below the one hundred after that, and there is nothing regarding the in-betweeners’.
And they<sup>asws</sup> both said: ‘Everything upon which the year has not passed by, so there is nothing upon it. So when the year does pass by, it would be Obligated upon it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah, Muhammad ibn Muslim, abu Basir, Burayd and al-Fudayl who have said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, and abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, have said, ‘

The amount of Zakat for sheep is one sheep for every forty sheep. There is not anything on what is less than forty. Thereafter there is no increase in Zakat up until it is one hundred twenty. Once it is more than one hundred twenty by one sheep, Zakat is two sheep; and Zakat is no more than two sheep until its number is two hundred. When it is more than two hundred by one sheep, then Zakat is three sheep. Thereafter there is no increase until it is three hundred and one sheep; in which case Zakat is four sheep. There is no increase until it is four hundred. When it is four hundred, then on every one hundred Zakat is one sheep and this supersedes the previous calculations. Thereafter Zakat is not due on what is less than one hundred or what is between the two taxable consecutive numbers.’
The two Imam have said, ‘Zakat is not due on whatever has not remained in the possession of its owner for one complete year. Once one year is complete, Zakat is obligatory.’”
